question: What is the annual income threshold for parents of government school students to enrol in private schools under the ‘Chirag’ scheme in Haryana?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Less than ₹1.8 lakh**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Less than ₹1.8 lakh** is the annual income threshold for parents of government school students to enrol in private schools under the 'Chirag' scheme in Haryana.
 
• The 'Chirag' scheme aims to provide quality education to children from economically weaker sections by allowing them to study in private schools.
 
• Under this scheme, the government covers the cost of education for eligible students in private schools.
 
• This initiative is part of the Haryana government's efforts to promote inclusive education and bridge the gap between different socio-economic groups.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The 'Chirag' scheme stands for **Chief Minister's Haryana Initiative for Revitalizing and Advancing of Government schools**.
 
• This scheme is part of a broader strategy to improve educational outcomes and infrastructure in the state.
 
• Parents need to provide proof of income to avail benefits under this scheme, ensuring that only eligible students benefit.
 
• The scheme also includes provisions for monitoring and evaluating the performance of students enrolled under it.
 
• The government collaborates with private schools to ensure that they adhere to the guidelines and provide quality education to the students.
